Mechanism of Action: Endogenous estrogens play a critical role in the development and maintenance of the female reproductive system and secondary sexual characteristics. Among circulating estrogens, estradiol is the primary intracellular estrogen in humans and exhibits significantly greater potency at the receptor level compared to its metabolites, estrone and estriol. In premenopausal women, the ovarian follicle is the main source of estrogen, secreting between 70 to 500 micrograms of estradiol daily, depending on the phase of the menstrual cycle. After menopause, most endogenous estrogen is derived from the peripheral conversion of androstenedione, secreted by the adrenal cortex, into estrone. Consequently, estrone and its sulfate-conjugated form, estrone sulfate, become the predominant circulating estrogens in postmenopausal women. Estrogens exert their effects by binding to nuclear receptors in estrogen-responsive tissues. To date, two types of estrogen receptors have been identified, and their distribution varies across different tissues. Circulating estrogens regulate the secretion of gonadotropins, luteinizing hormone (LH), and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) from the pituitary gland through a negative feedback mechanism. Estrogens help reduce the elevated levels of these hormones typically observed in postmenopausal women. Progestin compounds promote cellular differentiation and generally counteract the effects of estrogens. They achieve this by reducing estrogen receptor levels, increasing the local metabolism of estrogens into less active metabolites, or inducing gene products that diminish cellular responses to estrogen. Progestins exert their effects by binding to specific progesterone receptors, which interact with progesterone response elements in target genes. Progesterone receptors are found in the female reproductive tract, breast tissue, pituitary gland, hypothalamus, and central nervous system. Composition: A 5 mg dose of norethindrone acetate contains the following excipients: lactose monohydrate, corn starch, copovidone, talc, magnesium stearate, hypromellose, and triacetin. A 1 mg dose of norethindrone acetate contains the following excipients: lactose monohydrate, corn starch, hydroxypropyl cellulose, talc, magnesium stearate, hypromellose, and triacetin. Physical Properties: Estradiol (E2), an estrogen, is a white or nearly white crystalline powder. Norethindrone acetate (NETA), a progestin, is a white or yellowish-white crystalline powder.
